text: A factory uses a lot of energy.
But where does it actually go?
Number one: motors. Pumps, fans, and conveyors.
Two: compressed air, for tools, actuators, and cleaning.
Three: heating and cooling. Ovens, furnaces, chillers.
Four: machine tools. C N C machines, presses, moulding.
Five: lighting and the building, like air conditioning.
So how do engineers cut this energy?
They start early, at the design stage.
Lighter parts: less material to process and transport.
Fewer machining operations: less machine time.
Less friction in moving parts: less energy in use.
Better insulation: less heating and cooling.
Easy maintenance: the machine stays efficient for longer.
But be careful. The lowest energy process...
is not always the most sustainable product. Look at the whole life cycle.
Your turn. A part needs five machining steps. You redesign it to need three.
Which design fix is this? Pause now.
Fewer machining operations: less machine time.
Remember: every kilowatt hour counts.
